content:
# Solution

I'll create new bucket manifests and separate policy attachment files for each environment. The policy documents grant only `s3:GetObject` and `s3:PutObject` on the new logs bucket ARNs—not the existing assets bucket.

Since the existing User/Role names are not specified in the context, I've assumed `myapp` for both environments; adjust the `userName` and `roleName` fields if your existing IAM resources use different names.

---

`dev/logs-bucket.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: s3.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Bucket
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs-dev
spec:
  name: myapp-logs-dev
  versioningConfiguration:
    status: Enabled
  serverSideEncryptionConfiguration:
    rules:
    - applyServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
        sseAlgorithm: AES256
  publicAccessBlockConfiguration:
    blockPublicAcls: true
    ignorePublicAcls: true
    blockPublicPolicy: true
    restrictPublicBuckets: true
```

`dev/logs-policy.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: iam.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Policy
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs-policy-dev
spec:
  name: myapp-logs-policy-dev
  document: |
    {
      "Version": "2012-10-17",
      "Statement": [
        {
          "Effect": "Allow",
          "Action": [
            "s3:GetObject",
            "s3:PutObject"
          ],
          "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::myapp-logs-dev/*"
        }
      ]
    }
---
apiVersion: iam.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: UserPolicyAttachment
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs-attachment-dev
spec:
  policyName: myapp-logs-policy-dev
  userName: myapp
```

`prod/logs-bucket.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: s3.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Bucket
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs-prod
spec:
  name: myapp-logs-prod
  versioningConfiguration:
    status: Enabled
  serverSideEncryptionConfiguration:
    rules:
    - applyServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
        sseAlgorithm: AES256
  publicAccessBlockConfiguration:
    blockPublicAcls: true
    ignorePublicAcls: true
    blockPublicPolicy: true
    restrictPublicBuckets: true
```

`prod/logs-policy.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: iam.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Policy
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs-policy-prod
spec:
  name: myapp-logs-policy-prod
  document: |
    {
      "Version": "2012-10-17",
      "Statement": [
        {
          "Effect": "Allow",
          "Action": [
            "s3:GetObject",
            "s3:PutObject"
          ],
          "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::myapp-logs-prod/*"
        }
      ]
    }
---
apiVersion: iam.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: RolePolicyAttachment
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs-attachment-prod
spec:
  policyName: myapp-logs-policy-prod
  roleName: myapp
```

---

## Deployment

Apply each environment independently:
```bash
kubectl apply -f dev/logs-bucket.yaml dev/logs-policy.yaml
kubectl apply -f prod/logs-bucket.yaml prod/logs-policy.yaml
```

## Notes

- **User/Role references**: If your existing User (dev) or Role (prod) are named differently (e.g., `app-service-account`, `myapp-iam-role`), update `userName` and `roleName` fields accordingly.
- **Alternative**: If preferred, you can add the `Policy` and attachment resources directly to the existing `dev/iam.yaml` and `prod/iam.yaml` files instead of creating separate files. The end result is identical.
- **Principle of least privilege**: The policies are scoped to the logs bucket ARN only (`arn:aws:s3:::myapp-logs-{env}/*`), ensuring no unintended access to the assets bucket.
